findings.message: This is an instance fix. The defect class is: an expiry that the write will refuse is only found after the person has typed the Client secret and confirmed. `propose` now checks the kept expiry, but it does not check an `expiresAt` that the caller gives. When `a.expiresAt` is set, `propose` skips every check. Two inputs still get a confirm card and fail only at `run`. (1) A past day passes the `EXPIRY_DAY` regex, and then putSecret's `.refine(... > new Date(), "must be in the future")` refuses it (packages/core/src/secrets/manage.ts:30). (2) An impossible day such as `2026-13-45` also passes the regex, and `endOfDay` turns it into a string that fails `z.iso.datetime`. In both cases the person sees a zod validation error, not a refusal that says what to do. rotate_secret's `propose` (apps/web/lib/admin/secrets.ts:53-57) and put_secret's `propose` (line 43) have the same gap for a given `expiresAt`. Fix: add one shared check of a given day in `@amax/core/secrets` beside `endOfDay`. It should require a real calendar date whose end of day is still in the future, and throw a named refusal. Call it from every `propose` and `run` that takes `expiresAt`: set_github_app, put_secret and rotate_secret. Add a past date and an impossible date to the expiry-116 propose table.
findings.scenario: An Admin has an expired GitHub app and calls set_github_app with { clientId: 'Ov23liFAKEdemo02', expiresAt: '2025-01-31' }. propose resolves and the confirm card is shown. The Admin types the 40-character Client secret and confirms. putSecret then rejects with 'must be in the future', so the secret is discarded and the card fails. The same happens with expiresAt '2026-13-45'.

findings.message: `const endOf = endOfDay;` is a local alias that adds nothing. Delete it and call `endOfDay` directly at lines 47 and 62, as app-tool.ts does.
